newsitem.title: CONGO: Mandela arrives to chair Zaire peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Mandela arrives to chair Zaire peace talks.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela arrived in Congo on Wednesday to chair peace talks on a South African ship between Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila, witnesses said.
Mandela and United Nations and Organisation of African Unity special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun arrived in the Congolese port of Pointe Noire on Mandela's jet.
Mandela waited on his plane for 40 minutes before Congo President Pascal Lissouba arrived to welcome him. The two leaders then went to Lissouba's villa for a private meeting.
Lissouba told reporters as he arrived: "I don't know anything. I know less than you."

Mobutu and Kabila were scheduled to meet face-to-face for the second time at 11 a.m. (1000 gmt) aboard the South African navy icebreaker Outeniqua to discuss a transition to democracy after 32 years of autocratic rule by Mobutu.
By the scheduled starting time, there was no sign of Mobutu or Kabila, who was due to be brought by helicopter from the nearby port of Soyo.
A spokeswoman in Cape Town said Mandela was expected back in South Africa on Wednesday night.
